baseline: gptme release comparison: ordinary RPC and evaluation imports

review.archive_integrity: Verified both wheels against their RECORD hashes. 569 versus 574 members. METADATA differs only in Version; entry points and dependency declarations are unchanged.
review.imports: Both flagged DSPy files are byte-identical to 0.35.1. They import their own evaluation suites and slice EvalSpec lists for prompt optimization. There is no installation hook. Exact module/member imports already have canonical engine-emitted metadata/import/python findings, including aliases; no YAML shadow is needed.
review.retirement: Neither setup.py plus a dependency declaration nor an import named tests proves concealment, execution at import time, or even an external dependency. Retire both unsupported objective consumers with the redundant raw-text import matcher. Do not suppress tests imports by filename or package identity.
review.rpc: Both versions have a loopback-only bridge with a random 16-byte capability checked before pickle.loads, a registered-function dispatch table, and uint32-framed RPC replies. The bootstrap string connects to that local bridge and is sent to the Jupyter kernel by _exec_silent. It does not receive source for exec. New code adds automatic environment selection, uv/ipykernel fallback, displayhook message delivery and kernel memory-guard integration.
review.javascript: WorkspaceExplorer has identical file list/preview/download code after normalizing chunk references and three corresponding imported alias uses. Other UI changes include conversation cache separation by user, pagination, tool-result rendering and Tauri local-server connection handling. The new loopback URL uses a port returned by the desktop backend; no new external destination was introduced.
review.other_changes: New dirty_diff hook reads bounded git status/diff context, disables external diff and text conversion, redacts secret assignments, and marks repository text untrusted. Redaction moved from subagent/context.py to a shared utility. Other Python changes cover output metadata, review schema parsing, pre-commit runner selection, path expansion and editor argv handling.
review.placement: Move the unchanged connect-plus-uint32-unpack matcher to socket/framing, with a co-occurrence description and notable severity. Remove the unsupported T1105 mapping. Preserve the separate suspicious receive-plus-namespace-exec composite, whose description now states co-occurrence rather than proven flow.
review.consumers: No external YAML references the moved or retired exact IDs. The only supply-chain/install-hook ancestor consumer is a JavaScript-only Windsurf rule, incompatible with the retired Python rules. No YAML consumer selects the moved framing rule through an ancestor. The neutral target leaf already exists. The source file's other rule remains in place.

verification.controls: RPC and suite-import fixtures have no suspicious/hostile traits; socket-exec fixture retains suspicious receive-plus-namespace-exec detection.
